checks.value: by designing and selling hardware devices, and by delivering relevant online advertising

triage.note: ADR-003's normalization canon already ruled that raw newlines in HTML source collapse to a single space; nothing enforced it. Found by the T3 spike: 1 of 34 eval anchors was dead ('Microsoft was founded in 1975'), and the cause was not the anchor -- it was the normalizer preserving a source line-wrap that has no rendered meaning. Encoded as its own case rather than left to msft-2013-content because that case cannot discriminate at T3: with no segmentation, its text_contains checks fail on 'item not extracted' regardless of whether normalization is right or wrong.

provenance:
Microsoft FY2013 10-K (legacy HTML, 2001-2019 era), EDGAR accession 0001193125-13-310206 -- same fixture as msft-2013-structure/content. MEASURED with the throwaway T3 spike normalizer against the committed fixture on 2026-08-15. The filer's HTML is hard-wrapped at ~80 columns INSIDE text nodes: raw bytes at offset 43,815 read '...SIZE="2">Microsoft was founded in 1975. Our missi...' -- the newline is document-source formatting between two attributes' text, not a block boundary, and renders as a single space in any browser. Naive normalization (collapse horizontal whitespace, keep every newline) preserved it, so 858 mid-sentence line breaks survive in this fixture's normalized_text alone (regex [a-z,] ? [a-z]); nike-2006 has 669 by the same measure, and every other HTML/iXBRL fixture has 0 (aapl-2025, jpm-2024, cat-2023, nvda-2024, sandston-2021, premier-pacific-2016, malformed-html, aapl-2026-10q) -- so this is a filer/filing-agent style, present in exactly the mid-era HTML stratum, which is why the mid-era deep-tier fixture is the right host for the case. ANCHOR COUNTS (raw fixture, verified by direct substring count): 'Microsoft was founded in 1975' 1 occurrence in wrapped form, 0 in flat form; 'by designing and selling hardware devices, and by delivering relevant online advertising' 1 occurrence wrapped, 0 flat. Both are single-occurrence anchors -- the ideal per case-authoring step 4 -- and both are asserted here in their FLAT form, i.e. the case passes only if the normalizer rejoins them. The third check is the same fact stated negatively (the wrapped form must not survive), which is what makes this case impossible to satisfy by accident: a normalizer that deleted newlines entirely would pass the two positive checks, so 'ITEM 1. BUSINESS' is asserted as well -- that heading is produced ONLY by a real block boundary (raw: '

ITEM 1. BUSINESS

', with the space between ITEM and 1 coming from a   entity), so it simultaneously proves structural newlines still exist around it, proves   decoded to a real space and collapsed (the ADR-003 canon's third rule, the bug class that already bit this repo twice), and gives layer 4's line-anchored heading matcher something to match. NOTE FOR THE TXT ERA -- this ruling is format-era-scoped and must not be generalized: ge-1994 (2,178), ibm-1997 (1,798) and textron-2001 (353) show the same mid-sentence-newline signature, but there the newlines ARE the document's own fixed-width layout and are preserved by the passthrough policy (docs/architecture/overview.md layer 3); their anchors were authored line-locally and pass either way. ADR-006 records the split ruling. Authored 2026-08-15 at T3; watched red first (extract_items raised NotImplementedError).
